name: centroid_v1_20261013
status: written before any training run, any frozen-model substitution and any Qwen evaluation of the new rules; only the operator checks in checks/ had been run

input.request: fill in the experimental analysis of the Centroid / Centroid-2 reconstruction rule described there, on the training side

interpretation_decisions.cells_primary: The K+1 grid-centred rounding cells of the existing hard rule (Nearest, paper symbol CH): cell index l_j = r_j + 1[t_j >= 1/2], computed with exactly the arithmetic of the existing functions (bitwise check C10). Reasons: the description says the partition is that of the existing operator and only the representative changes; its table gives Nearest's representative as exp(cell centre), which holds only for these grid-centred cells; it gives the P index width as ceil(log2(K+1)) for Nearest and Centroid alike. Under this reading a K=4 operator has at most K+1=5 nonzero levels, the same budget as Nearest.
interpretation_decisions.cells_secondary: The K calibration intervals [b_r, b_{r+1}) (index r_j), K nonzero levels. Offline analyses only (substitution, row-level fidelity, Qwen); not trained.
interpretation_decisions.fw_tail: FW keeps the zero tail: keys with z < -tau are members of no cell and get weight 0, as in FW-Nearest/LERP. Cell-level mass conservation then holds for every in-window cell, the denominator equals Z restricted to the window, and the tail mass is lost exactly as in the existing FW operators. A variant that treats the tail as one extra centroid cell is offline-only (Qwen part, label C+tail).
interpretation_decisions.centroid2_numerics: count, sum(u), sum(u^2) with u = z - c_b (c_b the cell's grid centre); identical mean/variance, better conditioned fp32 sums. No clamping of the representative to the cell range (the description has none); the consequence is measured.
interpretation_decisions.range_grad: full, as in suite D. For both rules the output does not depend on the calibration statistics except through membership; checks C6 show full and detach give the same gradient to 1e-15 (fp64).
interpretation_decisions.implementation: per-cell sums by scatter_add over keys and gather back; on CUDA not bitwise reproducible run to run (atomic adds), like the MinMax gather backward of the existing runs. Same throughput as FW-Nearest Weight-STE (checks/check_gpu_step0.json).

code_root.path: code/centroid_root (copy of files_adaptive_quant_phaseB/code/phaseB_rr: model a cf76032a, quant a402460d, train 63a8001d) with approx centroid/centroid2 and --cells added
code_root.regression: every pre-existing path (softmax, exact_fp32_softmax, LERP, Nearest x MinMax/FW x detach/full x K 4/8) gives bitwise-identical loss and parameter gradients to phaseB_rr (check C9)

part_T_training.question: Can the new rule be pretrained from scratch at K=4, and where does it land relative to the same-calibration Nearest operators (Weight-STE, Prob-STE), LERP and softmax?
part_T_training.setting: 124M GPT (12x12x768), WikiText-103 (train/val sha 6c355b28.. / 397ae25d..), 100M tokens, block 1024, micro-batch 1, 131072 tokens/step, lr 6e-4 cosine to 0.1x, warmup 10M, AdamW (0.9,0.95) wd 0.1, clip 1.0, bf16 autocast outside the fp32 attention operator, TF32 on, seed 7, local RTX 3090, bta env (torch 2.5.1+cu121). Identical to the seed-7 suite-D controls and the round-3 baselines; in-training eval every 5M tokens on 100 batches (logging only).
part_T_training.evaluation: 20/40/60/80/100M checkpoints, own frozen root, full WikiText-103 validation (243 non-overlapping 1024-token blocks), batch 1, bf16 autocast outside the fp32 operator, TF32 off, local RTX 3090; geometry probe on the first 8 blocks (patched only to call the centroid reconstruct). Same evaluator protocol as the seed-7 controls in D_robustness_124m_100m_5seed/eval_native_v1 and supplement eval/local3090.
secondary_contrasts_100M: each Centroid-2 run - Exact and - same-calibration Prob-STE strict
part_T_training.descriptive: trajectories 20-100M vs Exact; training-log stability (non-finite values, largest loss increase between logs, grad norm); geometry at 100M (span, entropy, top-cell keys and mass); step-0 Q/K gradient norm

part_O_offline_124m.O1_substitution: Frozen suite-D Exact endpoints (100M, seeds 7/42/253/1337/2026). All 12 attention layers replaced at inference by rule x calibration x K: rules {Nearest (strict hard forward), LERP, Centroid, Centroid-2, Centroid-0 = exp(mean z) (the zero-variance term of Centroid-2), Centroid on interval cells}, calibration {MinMax, FW tau=6}, K {4,8,16,32}. Full validation (243 blocks), batch 1, bf16 autocast, TF32 off; Delta NLL vs the same model through the same analysis path with exact softmax. Reported per seed and as mean and SD over the five seeds.
part_O_offline_124m.O2_rows_and_gradients: First 4 validation blocks, all 12 layers and heads, exact forward and LM-loss backward of the frozen model supply S, V and the upstream dO of every attention output. For each rule x calibration x K in {2,4,8,16,32,64}: TV(P_hat, P), cell-level mass error on the Nearest cells, relative output error, and the score / dQ / dK gradient of the rule's backward (Centroid, Centroid-2: autograd; LERP: exact Jacobian; Nearest: Weight-STE and Prob-STE) contracted with the same dO, compared with the exact softmax gradient (cosine, relative L2). Also the within-cell contrast share of the exact score gradient, ||p_j (g_j - gbar_b)||^2 / ||p_j (g_j - <g>)||^2, i.e. the part a cell-averaged backward cannot represent; and per-cell representative statistics (lme - cell centre vs h^2/24; Centroid-2 log gap; share of cells whose Centroid-2 value exceeds the largest member weight). Models: Exact s7 at 20/40/60/80/100M, Exact 100M of the other four seeds, the seed-7 K4 endpoints of LERP, MinMax-Prob, FWM-Prob, FWM-Weight, and (after training) the four new runs.
part_O_offline_124m.role: mechanism and operator-level evidence only; never substitutes for the training result

part_Q_qwen.infrastructure: SideProject3/attention_coarsening2 (read only; its src is imported, nothing in it is modified). Same model revision, fp32 query-chunked reference path on layers {7,14,21}, other layers native sdpa, per-document mean NLL over all N-1 next tokens at N=2048 and 8192.

methods.A0: grid g_k=-6k/4, nearest grid point, zero below -6 (= FW-Nearest K4 tau 6)
methods.C0: exp(mean z) on the A0 cells
methods.C-int: Centroid on the 4 interval cells of [-6,0]
methods.C+tail: Centroid on the A0 cells plus the tail z<-6 as one more centroid cell (full mass conservation)

part_Q_qwen.statistics: document-level paired bootstrap, 10000 resamples, seed 20261013, 2K and 8K of a document resampled together, 95% percentile intervals; contrasts C-A0, C-exact_ref, C2-C, C0-C, C-int-C, C+tail-C, A0-exact_ref
part_Q_qwen.regression: exact_ref per-token NLL on these documents must equal the stored stage-4 exact_ref values bitwise (cache/nll_tail_g1_rep/exact_ref)
part_Q_qwen.Q2_local: captured rows of its first-round test split (32 documents x 2 lengths x 32 rows, layers 7/14/21, all heads): post-W_O joint squared error of A0, C, C2, C0, C-int on the FW grid tau=6 for K in {4,8,16}; error reduction relative to A0 and the C0-vs-C and C2-vs-C gaps as functions of K

statistics_training: circular moving-block bootstrap over the 243 per-block NLL differences, block 16, 4000 resamples, RNG 20260920 re-seeded per contrast, 95% percentile; identical to the round-3 analysis. These intervals cover validation-sample uncertainty only, not training randomness.
